questions.question: Why did Tomek feel like a stranger in Nikiszowiec as a child?
answers: Because he didn't know the Silesian dialect
Because the new estate and its layout seemed to him a trap of red brick
Because he wanted to work in the mine right away
Because he didn't like churches
questions.explanation: The beginning of the text emphasizes the move, the foreignness of the place and the feeling of being trapped.

questions.question: Where does Tomek first see the figure of the Black Monk?
answers: At the station in Katowice
By the Church of St. Anne, in the shadow of a gate
On the roof of a family tenement block
In the mine lift
questions.explanation: The first meeting takes place by the Church of St. Anne, next to one of the gates.

questions.question: What role does the Gisze/Wieczorek mine play in the text?
answers: It is only an insignificant backdrop
It is the breadwinner mother and the source of the residents' fate
It is a museum visited by tourists
It is described as a private gallery
questions.explanation: The text says directly that the mine gave work, homes and decided the residents' lives.

questions.question: What does the Monk's gesture mean during the second meeting with Tomek?
answers: An invitation to descend underground
A pointing to the church and to the memory of the place
A threat against the residents
A request for money
questions.explanation: The Monk points to the church, and Tomek reads it as a sign of memory of those who passed.

questions.question: How does Tomek's attitude towards Nikiszowiec change at the end of the story?
answers: He still wants to escape from there
He begins to see it as a home and a guide to his own history
He decides to sell his parents' flat
He stops believing in any legends
questions.explanation: From a place-trap, Nikiszowiec becomes his home and a carrier of memory.
